rated a book it was amazing The Long Ships by Frans G. Bengtsson
I love good historical fiction that brings an era to life, and this did this with the viking era magically well. I understand their need to plunder, and their desire to farm and live the good life better, and tension between those. If you run out of I love good historical fiction that brings an era to life, and this did this with the viking era magically well. I understand their need to plunder, and their desire to farm and live the good life better, and tension between those. If you run out of money, you have to go plunder more!

I loved the descriptions of the voyages and how dangerous and hard they were. And then if you successfully found some plunder, the trip home was almost more dangerous as other vikings were out there trying to steal your plunder.

"The pork was rancid, the stockfish mildewed, the meal stale, the bread maggoty, and the water sour; but Krok and those of his followers who had sailed on expeditions of this sort before asserted that this was as good fare as any sailor could wish for."

I think my favorite part is when Orm becomes a slave galley rower for several years. The descriptions of that hard life, how he survived it, and how much it toughened him are the stuff of legends. I think many successful people have a "thrown into the fire" moment that made them who they are, and this was as good a one as any I've heard. It's also worth remarking how many slaves there were back then, and off all races. Slavery was commonplace in a world where there is no law and order.

"Viking" is actually a verb not a noun, and "to go viking" it means to go adventure and plunder. It became a lifestyle and part of their culture, which is well encapsulated by this sentence that Orm speaks as he goes on a viking trip after a long break:

"I cannot understand why I have kept away from the sea for so long,” he said, “for a well-manned ship is the best of all things. It is good to sit contented ashore, and no man need be ashamed to do so; but a voyage to a far land, with booty awaiting a man and this smell in his nostrils, is as good a lot as could be desired, and a sure cure for age and sorrow." ...more
